### Codebase evidence

- `src/perk/cli/stages.py::make_stage_launcher` — the one `--remote` option/help for generated
  launchers; `MergedCommand.get_help` renders the launcher half's help for `pr submit`/`pr land`/
  `plan save`.
- `src/perk/run/launch/worktree.py::resolve_target` — raises `UserFacingCliError`
  (`remote_blocked`, "stage '<id>' is local-only (cold_remote:false)") when `--remote` hits a
  `cold_remote:false` stage; pinned by `tests/test_cli_stages.py` (plan + objective-author arms)
  and `tests/test_launch.py`.
- `src/perk/cli/commands/plan/resume_cmd.py` — `--remote` help is the generic string; resume
  forwards `remote` into `launch_stage`, so a gate/learn-resolved stage rejects at launch.
- No test pins the generic help string ("Local (default)" has zero hits under `tests/`), so the
  help change is safe; `tests/test_registry.py::` census (line asserting
  `cold_remote == {"implement", "address"}`) is the registry-side guard and stays untouched.

## Changes

### 1. `docs/user-docs/explanation/how-perk-thinks.md` — the claims rewrite

- **"Why this shape" payoff paragraph** (first of the three): replace the "resumable from
  anywhere, by anyone, on any machine" paragraph with the settled claim triple, keeping the
  "two views of one design" energy but scoped honestly:
  - Because the plan is durable and canonical and every stage has a cold local door, **every
    stage is locally resumable** — from any machine, by anyone, with nothing more than the repo
    and the plan id.
  - The **bounded agentic stages** — `implement` and `address`, where the goal is already pinned
    by a plan or by reviewer feedback — are additionally **remotely headless-able**: the same
    cold door pointed at a CI runner.
  - The **human gates stay local**: `submit`, `land`, and `learn` are local-only by design —
    review, merge, and judgment capture are deliberately kept where a human is.
  - Keep a one-clause pointer that resumability and the remote door are the same property at two
    scopes, not two features.
- **"Stages and doors" re-entry paragraph**: qualify "re-enter exactly where you were" and define
  the **WIP durability boundary** here (this is the canonical definition site):
  - What carries across machines/sessions is **stage-boundary + pushed-branch durability**: the
    saved plan and its progress (canonical tier) plus any branch pushed to `origin`.
  - **Uncommitted local edits (and unpushed commits) in a worktree are explicitly outside the
    cross-machine contract** — they live only on the machine that made them. Resume re-enters
    the *stage*, not the keystrokes.
  - Cross-link `recover-a-dirty-worktree.md` as the recipe when local WIP is in the way.
- **State-tiers section**: append the boundary clause to the "delete a worktree, switch machines,
  or hand a plan to a colleague, and nothing important is lost" sentence — "nothing *canonical* is
  lost; uncommitted worktree edits are the one thing that is machine-local" (one clause, pointing
  at the doors-section definition; do not duplicate the full boundary).
- **Maturity paragraph** ("Running a stage somewhere else"): replace "newest and least-proven /
  not yet fully proven / emerging rather than battle-tested" with the current truth, matching the
  language every other maturity site adopted at 2.2: the live end-to-end chain (real `implement` +
  `address` runs) is **proven on perk's own repo**; the **consumer-repo** remote drive remains
  execution-untested. Keep the existing pointer to `headless-and-remote.md` as the depth page.
- Leave the "Not every stage gets a remote door" paragraph's rationale intact (it already matches
  the claim triple); tighten only if wording collides with the new payoff text.

### 2. `docs/user-docs/how-to/recover-a-dirty-worktree.md` — align with the boundary

Add one short framing (intro paragraph after the two friction bullets, or a "Watch out" bullet —
implementer's choice of position, content fixed): uncommitted changes are **outside perk's
cross-machine durability contract** — durable state is the saved plan plus pushed branches;
commit (and submit/push) is what promotes local WIP into the durable tier. Link back to
[How perk thinks → stages and doors] for the boundary definition. No step changes.

### 3. `skills/perk-expert/references/mental-model.md` — the self-contained mirror

- §3 operator rule: append the WIP-boundary clause to "You can delete a worktree, switch machines,
  or hand a plan to a colleague without losing anything important" — scoped to canonical state +
  pushed branches; uncommitted worktree edits are machine-local.
- §4: add the payoff claim triple in compact form (every stage locally resumable; `implement`/
  `address` remotely runnable; `submit`/`land`/`learn` local-only human-gate stages) — §4 already
  names the remote set and the maturity state, so this is a sentence-level addition, not a section.
- Footer's "Canonical source" line unchanged.

### 4. CLI help — one seam, scope-aware (`src/perk/cli/stages.py`)

- In `make_stage_launcher`, derive the `--remote` help from the stage's door:
  - `cold_remote:true` → keep `"Local (default) or a remote runner (dispatch the stage to CI)."`
  - `cold_remote:false` → `f"Local (default) or a remote runner; '{stage.id}' is local-only (cold_remote:false)."`
    (the same phrasing family as every dedicated local-only command).
  - Decision: **keep the `--remote` flag on local-only launchers** (uniform launcher surface; the
    friendly `remote_blocked` runtime rejection is already the tested contract) — only the help
    text changes. Removing the flag would turn a helpful exit-1 error into Click's exit-2
    no-such-option and break the tested error vocabulary.
- In `src/perk/cli/commands/plan/resume_cmd.py`, scope the `--remote` help for the stage-dynamic
  resume: `"Local (default) or a remote runner (dispatch the resolved stage to CI; only the remotely runnable stages — implement/address — dispatch)."`
  (exact wording may be trimmed to fit one line; must name implement/address).
- **Test pin**: extend `tests/test_cli_stages.py` with one help-census test asserting
  (a) `perk pr submit --help`, `perk pr land --help`, and `perk plan save --help` each carry
  `local-only (cold_remote:false)` in the `--remote` help, and (b) `perk implement --help` and
  `perk pr address --help` do **not** — keyed off the registry doors so the census can't drift
  from `tests/test_registry.py`'s `{"implement", "address"}` pin.

### 5. `shared/registry.yaml` — settle the stale `cold_remote` comment

Rewrite the `doors.cold_remote` comment block (currently "P2.T8c flips it true… Phase 2 builds…;
Phase 3 drives it. Revisable in Phase 3.") to the settled statement, breadcrumb-free per the
comment-hygiene convention: `cold_remote` records which stages a remote runner may run — `true`
exactly on the bounded agentic stages (`implement`, `address`); the interactive/exploratory stages
and the quick deterministic human-gate ops (`submit`/`land`/`learn`) are local-only **by design**
(keep the `cli-vs-pi §4.5` reference; it is a contracts-style pointer, not a breadcrumb). Also
strip the two inline `# P2.T8c: a Phase-3 CI worker can run it` comments on the `implement`/
`address` door lines (replace with `# bounded agentic stage — remotely runnable`). Data untouched;
`tests/test_registry.py` census unaffected.

### 6. `docs/user-docs/reference/cli.md` — state the scope

- Common-flags paragraph: extend the `--remote` clause with the scope — only the remotely
  runnable stages (`implement`, `address`) dispatch; every other launcher rejects `--remote` as
  local-only.
- The "Stage launchers (the earned flat names)" intro ("accepts `--worktree`, `--dry-run`, and
  `--remote`"): add the same one-clause scope note.
- `pr submit`, `pr land`, `plan save` entries: add "Local-only (`cold_remote:false`)" in the
  launcher-half sentence, mirroring the existing local-only entries' convention.
- `plan resume` entry: "`--remote` dispatches to CI" → note it applies only when the resolved
  stage is remotely runnable (`implement`/`address`); gate and `learn` outcomes stay local.

### 7. Audit pass over the named remaining docs (update only where stale)

Per the doc-accuracy gate (`docs/learned/workflow/doc-reconciliation.md`): grep the claim phrases
and render live `--help` for cited surfaces; change nothing that is already true.

- `headless-and-remote.md`: expected **no-op** (2.2/3.1 already rewrote it); verify the
  "What is identical / what differs" list still matches contracts §8.38 and the new payoff wording.
- `resume-a-plan.md` step 4: name the remote set — "Only the unattended stages (`implement`,
  `address`) are remotely runnable" (matches `dispatch-a-stage-to-ci.md`).
- `set-up-the-remote-runner.md`, `dispatch-a-stage-to-ci.md`, `supervise-dispatched-runs.md`,
  `advance-an-objective-headlessly.md`, `explanation/index.md`, `reference/in-session.md`:
  expected **no-op**; verify only.

## Boundaries / non-goals

- **No mechanism changes.** No registry *data* change, no door/`resolve_target` behavior change,
  no new flags; the only code edits are help strings + one test.
- **No re-documenting of features** — prior nodes own the feature docs; this node touches claims.
- **No contracts.md changes** — §8.36–§8.38 already state the cross-plane behavior; nothing here
  changes behavior. (If the audit finds a contracts sentence contradicting the claim triple, flag
  it in the PR rather than silently amending.)
- **No checkpoint/durable-WIP machinery** — the boundary is documented, not mechanized (objective
  boundary).
- `docs/learned/workflow/remote-runner.md` is a learned doc, already softened at 2.2 — out of scope.

## Steps

1. Rewrite `how-perk-thinks.md` (payoff triple, WIP durability boundary definition, state-tiers
   clause, maturity paragraph).
2. Align `recover-a-dirty-worktree.md` (boundary framing + cross-link).
3. Mirror in `skills/perk-expert/references/mental-model.md` (§3 clause, §4 triple).
4. Scope-aware `--remote` help in `make_stage_launcher` + `resume_cmd`; help-census test in
   `tests/test_cli_stages.py`.
5. Settle the `shared/registry.yaml` `cold_remote` comment block (comments only).
6. Update `reference/cli.md` (common flags, flat-launcher intro, `pr submit`/`pr land`/`plan save`
   entries, `plan resume` entry).
7. Audit pass over `headless-and-remote.md` + the resume/remote/supervision how-tos +
   `in-session.md`; fix `resume-a-plan.md` step 4; leave the rest unless stale.
8. `just ci` green.

## Acceptance

- `grep -rn "resumable from anywhere, by anyone, on any machine" docs/ skills/` → no hits;
  `grep -rn "emerging rather than battle-tested\|least-proven" docs/user-docs` → no hits.
- The WIP durability boundary is defined once in `how-perk-thinks.md`, echoed in
  `recover-a-dirty-worktree.md` and `mental-model.md`.
- `perk pr submit --help`, `perk pr land --help`, `perk plan save --help`, and the dedicated
  local-only launchers all state `local-only (cold_remote:false)` for `--remote`;
  `perk implement --help` / `perk pr address --help` do not — pinned by the new census test.
- Registry data untouched (`tests/test_registry.py` unchanged and green); `just ci` green.

", "plan_body": "# Reconcile the resumability/headless claims in the user docs to the guarantee the code now provides

Part of Objective #1093, Node 3.2.

## Context

Objective #1093 ("Make the resumability and headless claims true") has landed all six mechanism
nodes: canonical `learn_state` (1.1, PR #1097), the shared `NextAction` classifier (1.2, PR #1105),
canonical GHA run discovery (1.3, PR #1111), worker extension loading (2.1, PR #1116), the live
remote E2E proof (2.2, PR #1129), and the §8.38 parity tests (3.1, PR #1132). This final node
reconciles only the **top-level claims** — the payoff paragraphs, the WIP durability boundary, and
the `cold_remote` scope statement — rather than re-documenting features (each prior node already
updated its affected docs in the same turn, per repo convention).

The settled claim triple (the objective's design decision): **every stage is locally resumable;
the bounded agentic stages (`implement`, `address`) are remotely headless-able; human gates stay
local** (`submit`/`land`/`learn` are local-only by design).

## Findings

### Status — what is stale today (verified against the tree)

1. **`docs/user-docs/explanation/how-perk-thinks.md`** carries three stale/over-strong claims:
   - The "Why this shape" payoff paragraph: *"the workflow is **resumable from anywhere, by
     anyone, on any machine.** … Resumability and the remote door are two views of one design."*
     Too strong as written — the remote door covers only `implement`/`address`.
   - The "Stages and doors" re-entry paragraph: *"You can stop, come back tomorrow, and re-enter
     exactly where you were"* — no WIP durability boundary; uncommitted worktree edits do NOT
     carry across machines.
   - The maturity paragraph in "Running a stage somewhere else": *"the newest and least-proven
     part of perk … live, end-to-end execution is not yet fully proven. Treat it as **emerging
     rather than battle-tested**"* — stale since Node 2.2's live proof (2026-07-04). Every other
     remote-maturity doc site was already softened by PR #1129; this page was deliberately left
     for this node.
   - The state-tiers section's *"you can delete a worktree, switch machines … and nothing
     important is lost"* also lacks the uncommitted-edits caveat.
2. **The WIP durability boundary exists nowhere in the docs.** `grep -rn "stage boundary|stage-boundary"
   docs/user-docs skills/perk-expert` → no hits. `recover-a-dirty-worktree.md` describes the dirty-tree
   *frictions* (submit refuses, wipe skips) but never frames uncommitted edits as outside the
   cross-machine durability contract.
3. **CLI help contradicts the `cold_remote` scope on the merged/hidden launchers.**
   `make_stage_launcher` (`src/perk/cli/stages.py`) hard-codes one `--remote` help string —
   `"Local (default) or a remote runner (dispatch the stage to CI)."` — for every stage. All ten
   registry stages are in `DEDICATED_STAGES`, so this generic launcher surfaces only via the
   merged commands (`perk pr submit`, `perk pr land`, `perk plan save` — launcher halves built by
   `make_merged_command`) and the `learn` group's hidden bare launcher — **all four of which are
   `cold_remote:false`**. Their `--help` therefore implies remote dispatch works; runtime rejects
   with `remote_blocked` (`src/perk/run/launch/worktree.py::resolve_target`). Every *dedicated*
   local-only command already states the scope in its help (e.g. `objective plan`: *"…; objective
   plan is local-only (cold_remote:false)."* — same pattern in `plan replan/from`, `objective
   author/save/replan`, `learn docs/code`).
4. **`docs/user-docs/reference/cli.md`** has three scope gaps: the common-flags paragraph
   ("launcher commands accept … `--remote` (dispatch the stage to a CI runner…)") states no scope;
   the `pr submit` / `pr land` / `plan save` entries carry no "local-only" note (unlike every other
   local-only launcher entry, which says "Local-only (`cold_remote:false`)"); the `plan resume`
   entry says "`--remote` dispatches to CI" without noting only remotely-runnable resolved stages
   dispatch.

", "plan_body": "# Reconcile the resumability/headless claims in the user docs to the guarantee the code now provides

Part of Objective #1093, Node 3.2.

## Context

Objective #1093 ("Make the resumability and headless claims true") has landed all six mechanism
nodes: canonical `learn_state` (1.1, PR #1097), the shared `NextAction` classifier (1.2, PR #1105),
canonical GHA run discovery (1.3, PR #1111), worker extension loading (2.1, PR #1116), the live
remote E2E proof (2.2, PR #1129), and the §8.38 parity tests (3.1, PR #1132). This final node
reconciles only the **top-level claims** — the payoff paragraphs, the WIP durability boundary, and
the `cold_remote` scope statement — rather than re-documenting features (each prior node already
updated its affected docs in the same turn, per repo convention).

The settled claim triple (the objective's design decision): **every stage is locally resumable;
the bounded agentic stages (`implement`, `address`) are remotely headless-able; human gates stay
local** (`submit`/`land`/`learn` are local-only by design).

## Findings

### Status — what is stale today (verified against the tree)

1. **`docs/user-docs/explanation/how-perk-thinks.md`** carries three stale/over-strong claims:
   - The "Why this shape" payoff paragraph: *"the workflow is **resumable from anywhere, by
     anyone, on any machine.** … Resumability and the remote door are two views of one design."*
     Too strong as written — the remote door covers only `implement`/`address`.
   - The "Stages and doors" re-entry paragraph: *"You can stop, come back tomorrow, and re-enter
     exactly where you were"* — no WIP durability boundary; uncommitted worktree edits do NOT
     carry across machines.
   - The maturity paragraph in "Running a stage somewhere else": *"the newest and least-proven
     part of perk … live, end-to-end execution is not yet fully proven. Treat it as **emerging
     rather than battle-tested**"* — stale since Node 2.2's live proof (2026-07-04). Every other
     remote-maturity doc site was already softened by PR #1129; this page was deliberately left
     for this node.
   - The state-tiers section's *"you can delete a worktree, switch machines … and nothing
     important is lost"* also lacks the uncommitted-edits caveat.
2. **The WIP durability boundary exists nowhere in the docs.** `grep -rn "stage boundary|stage-boundary"
   docs/user-docs skills/perk-expert` → no hits. `recover-a-dirty-worktree.md` describes the dirty-tree
   *frictions* (submit refuses, wipe skips) but never frames uncommitted edits as outside the
   cross-machine durability contract.
3. **CLI help contradicts the `cold_remote` scope on the merged/hidden launchers.**
   `make_stage_launcher` (`src/perk/cli/stages.py`) hard-codes one `--remote` help string —
   `"Local (default) or a remote runner (dispatch the stage to CI)."` — for every stage. All ten
   registry stages are in `DEDICATED_STAGES`, so this generic launcher surfaces only via the
   merged commands (`perk pr submit`, `perk pr land`, `perk plan save` — launcher halves built by
   `make_merged_command`) and the `learn` group's hidden bare launcher — **all four of which are
   `cold_remote:false`**. Their `--help` therefore implies remote dispatch works; runtime rejects
   with `remote_blocked` (`src/perk/run/launch/worktree.py::resolve_target`). Every *dedicated*
   local-only command already states the scope in its help (e.g. `objective plan`: *"…; objective
   plan is local-only (cold_remote:false)."* — same pattern in `plan replan/from`, `objective
   author/save/replan`, `learn docs/code`).
4. **`docs/user-docs/reference/cli.md`** has three scope gaps: the common-flags paragraph
   ("launcher commands accept … `--remote` (dispatch the stage to a CI runner…)") states no scope;
   the `pr submit` / `pr land` / `plan save` entries carry no "local-only" note (unlike every other
   local-only launcher entry, which says "Local-only (`cold_remote:false`)"); the `plan resume`
   entry says "`--remote` dispatches to CI" without noting only remotely-runnable resolved stages
   dispatch.

updated its affected docs in the same turn, per repo convention).

the bounded agentic stages (`implement`, `address`) are remotely headless-able; human gates stay
local** (`submit`/`land`/`learn` are local-only by design).

## Findings

### Status — what is stale today (verified against the tree)

1. **`docs/user-docs/explanation/how-perk-thinks.md`** carries three stale/over-strong claims:
   - The "Why this shape" payoff paragraph: *"the workflow is **resumable from anywhere, by
     anyone, on any machine.** … Resumability and the remote door are two views of one design."*
     Too strong as written — the remote door covers only `implement`/`address`.
   - The "Stages and doors" re-entry paragraph: *"You can stop, come back tomorrow, and re-enter
     exactly where you were"* — no WIP durability boundary; uncommitted worktree edits do NOT
     carry across machines.
   - The maturity paragraph in "Running a stage somewhere else": *"the newest and least-proven
     part of perk … live, end-to-end execution is not yet fully proven. Treat it as **emerging
     rather than battle-tested**"* — stale since Node 2.2's live proof (2026-07-04). Every other
     remote-maturity doc site was already softened by PR #1129; this page was deliberately left
     for this node.

     important is lost"* also lacks the uncommitted-edits caveat.
2. **The WIP durability boundary exists nowhere in the docs.** `grep -rn "stage boundary|stage-boundary"
   docs/user-docs skills/perk-expert` → no hits. `recover-a-dirty-worktree.md` describes the dirty-tree
   *frictions* (submit refuses, wipe skips) but never frames uncommitted edits as outside the
   cross-machine durability contract.
3. **CLI help contradicts the `cold_remote` scope on the merged/hidden launchers.**
   `make_stage_launcher` (`src/perk/cli/stages.py`) hard-codes one `--remote` help string —
   `"Local (default) or a remote runner (dispatch the stage to CI)."` — for every stage. All ten
   registry stages are in `DEDICATED_STAGES`, so this generic launcher surfaces only via the
   merged commands (`perk pr submit`, `perk pr land`, `perk plan save` — launcher halves built by

   with `remote_blocked` (`src/perk/run/launch/worktree.py::resolve_target`). Every *dedicated*
   local-only command already states the scope in its help (e.g. `objective plan`: *"…; objective
   plan is local-only (cold_remote:false)."* — same pattern in `plan replan/from`, `objective
   author/save/replan`, `learn docs/code`).

   the `pr submit` / `pr land` / `plan save` entries carry no "local-only" note (unlike every other

   dispatch.

  wrong — prior nodes already updated them; this node's how-to work is an audit plus two
  sentence-level alignments (`resume-a-plan.md`, `recover-a-dirty-worktree.md`).

    stage is locally resumable** — from any machine, by anyone, with nothing more than the repo

    cross-machine contract** — they live only on the machine that made them. Resume re-enters

  `address` runs) is **proven on perk's own repo**; the **consumer-repo** remote drive remains
  execution-untested. Keep the existing pointer to `headless-and-remote.md` as the depth page.

  the claim triple); tighten only if wording collides with the new payoff text.

### 2. `docs/user-docs/how-to/recover-a-dirty-worktree.md` — align with the boundary

Add one short framing (intro paragraph after the two friction bullets, or a "Watch out" bullet —
implementer's choice of position, content fixed): uncommitted changes are **outside perk's
cross-machine durability contract** — durable state is the saved plan plus pushed branches;
